description: We're a team of CS students from Amman, Jordan, who love building real products fast, from mobile apps to AI and data-driven tools. Our goal for Space Apps is to turn NASA data into a working prototype that actually helps people, not just a pitch. We're looking for teammates who are into data analysis, UI/UX design, or storytelling and presenting
summary: Satellites change, but fires do not. When NASA's fire detections switch from MODIS to the sharper VIIRS cameras, raw fire counts jump (in the Levant, 6.0× from 2011 to 2012, while Aqua-MODIS alone saw 0.95×), so a satellite change can look like a change in fires. F.I.R.E.S. harmonizes NASA FIRMS data from Aqua MODIS, Suomi NPP, NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 onto one consistent Aqua MODIS equivalent scale, giving a weekly burning activity calendar for 2003–2026 for any area on Earth. Every number shows its 90% uncertainty range and its baseline, and missing data is never shown as zero fire. The app also shows the season, unusual weeks, how this week compares with past years, and a calibrated 7-day outlook. It matters now because Suomi NPP stopped on 2 November 2026 and MODIS is nearing the end of its life: without harmonization, NASA's long fire record breaks. The app works in English and Arabic.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Pick a named area (the Levant, Jordan, Argentina, the Northern Jordan forest belt, the Paraná Delta) or draw a box anywhere on Earth, and read its fire year week by week, on one Aqua MODIS equivalent scale of fire cell days, with a 90% uncertainty range. The app adds the seasonal profile, critical periods, unusual weeks, "this week vs history", and a calibrated 7 day chance of satellite detected fire per 0.25° cell, shown next to a persistence baseline. The interface works in English and Arabic (right-to-left).

HOW IT WORKS

We keep confident vegetation fire detections from NASA FIRMS and count fire cell days per satellite. Satellites are never added together. We link each satellite to Aqua MODIS: NOAA-20 to Suomi NPP (ratio 0.994, no correction needed), NOAA-21 to Suomi NPP (x1.027), and Suomi NPP to Aqua-equivalent with region x month ratios. Every link is tested on held out years.

RESULTS (held out tests)

- Suomi NPP to Aqua equivalent error (WAPE): 0.086, versus 0.242 for one global ratio.

- 90% ranges covered 90.7-92.0% of held out years.

- 7-day outlook, test block 2-30 October 2026: ROC-AUC 0.880 versus 0.749 for persistence. (ROC-AUC is a ranking measure, not accuracy.)

- We tested Terra to Aqua against a rule fixed in advance. It failed (0.136 vs 0.086), so Terra is shown per sensor and not forced onto the scale.

- We measured Aqua's orbit drift (observed/predicted 0.905 in 2026), so from 2022 VIIRS carries the scale.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Fair year to year comparison of burning activity for fire and land managers, forestry and civil protection planners, and researchers, and a record that survives the end of MODIS. It is free to run: free NASA data, open source code, an ordinary PC.

HONEST LIMITS

Clouds are not mapped (a low count can mean cloud, not no fire). Counts are detected fire, not burned area. No weather inputs yet. The risk outlook is a planning aid, not an ignition forecast, and the risk model is trained on 2026 data. Details are in the repository: docs/METHODOLOGY.md, DATA_CARD.md, MODEL_CARD.md.

TOOLS

Python, a local web API and a Leaflet web app, NASA FIRMS data, and an optional 3D globe built on gods-eye-view.

Extended walkthrough video (5 min, narrated in English, optional extra): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Wpa-vHAL6kBBT1beeisFbxiSegGXuNZs/view?usp=sharing
